title: Runtime warmup protector and gradual degrade strategy for attention kernels
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Recent rollouts of FlashAttention v3 variants and aggressive kernel-probing at startup have caused spikes in prefill latency and transient OOMs for long-context customers. The runtime currently probes kernels aggressively during model cold-start which can thrash workspace allocation and evict useful KV cache entries.

Goal: Implement a "warmup protector" and a gradual degradation strategy that: (1) gates speculative kernel probes behind a rate-limited wavefront, (2) protects KV cache priming during the first N prefills, and (3) provides immediate, predictable fallbacks to stable v2-compatible kernels when resource pressure is detected. The solution must be observable, toggleable via config, and safe to rollback without requiring global model restarts.

Scope: Kernel selection layer, prefill pacing, KV cache priming heuristics, and rollout guards. Not in scope: model-level quantization changes and allocator redesign (separate follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: Warmup protector implemented: speculative kernel probes are rate-limited per-host and per-model and visible in runtime telemetry.
KV cache priming: first 3 prefills for a model reserve a small eviction budget so hot prefixes are preserved during startup.
Fallback behavior: when memory thrashing or increased prefill P50 latency (>30% over baseline) is observed for 60s, runtime switches to a defined stable kernel path automatically.
No regression in stable 99p latency for long-context internal benchmarks (<=1% change).
Feature is behind a runtime flag and can be globally disabled and fully rolled back without restarting running sessions.
implementation_notes: Add 'warmup_wavefront' token bucket per model-shard: burst=3 probes, rate=1 probe/5s (configurable).
Introduce KV priming lease: during first N prefills (config default N=3) hold eviction budget of 5% of workspace to keep prefetched keys stable.
Integrate a lightweight prober that uses historical matrix-profile to decide whether to try v3 kernels; avoid probing heavy multitoken prefill for >2 tokens at once.
Expose telemetry hooks: probe_attempt, probe_success, probe_failure, kv_eviction_pressure, probe_fallback_reason. Hook into Console rollouts dashboard.
Add a health check that watches working set churn and prefill latency; if thresholds breached, flip 'stable-path' tag for subsequent requests for 60s and emit incident metric.
technical_decision_log: 2026-03-10: Decided to use per-model-shard rate limiting rather than global rate limits to avoid head-of-line effects across tenants (Aisha/Khoi).
2026-03-11: Chose a conservative default for probe rate (1 per 5s) after bench runs showing 4x workspace churn at higher probe rates (Connor).
2026-03-12: Rejected prefill-timeout-based protection because timeouts vary widely across models; opted for eviction-budget approach to protect KV cache (Lena).
2026-03-13: Rollout safety: feature behind a runtime flag + coordinated canary (2% traffic) with automatic rollback on SLO breach >0.5% for 10m (Priya).
testing_plan: Unit tests for token-bucket and KV eviction-lease logic.
Integration harness: simulate 500 concurrent cold-start prefill streams and assert no OOMs with and without feature.
A/B canary: 2% traffic on runtime-1.22 for 24h, monitor prefill P50/P95/P99 and working set churn metrics.
Chaos test: artificially constrain GPU workspace to force eviction and validate immediate fallback correctness and metric emission.
Add regression test in perf-suite to assert 99p latency < baseline+1% for long-context eval prompts.
rollout_plan: Feature implementation merged behind feature flag (PR link below).
Internal dogfood: enable for infra-staging with synthetic workloads; run 24h soak with perf and OOM dashboard checks.
Canary: enable for 2% of host pool (low-traffic customers) for 24h; automatic rollback if SLO breach detected.
Gradual ramp: 2% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with 12h observation windows between ramps.
If any stage triggers rollback: disable feature flag and notify on-call; create postmortem if customer-impacting.
